why: Although it sits in the backtracking week, plain backtracking over 10^5 digits is hopeless. The structure is greedy: build the answer left to right, trying the largest digit first, and keep it only if the remaining digits can still be arranged. Backtracking's 'try, check, undo' becomes a fast feasibility test.
hints: Lexicographically largest means: make the first character as large as possible, then the second, and so on, as long as the rest can still be completed. What makes the rest completable?

Split digits into high (5-9) and low (0-4). Two highs can never be adjacent (sum >= 10), and a high v needs both neighbours <= 9 - v. So each high needs its own slot between suitable lows; feasibility is a counting check on how many highs of value >= v fit next to lows <= 9 - v.

Greedy: at each position try digits 9 down to 0 that fit next to the previous digit, and accept the first whose removal leaves a feasible multiset (O(10 * 5) counting check). Once no highs remain, append the lows in descending order. O(n * 100).
pitfalls: Return the empty string when even the full multiset is infeasible, e.g. "889".
Leading zeros are kept: the answer is a string, not a number.
Descending order is not always valid: "188" must become "818", not "881".
Trying full backtracking with undo will time out at n = 10^5.
